rules.name: A Candle 2 closure is always a reversal closure that sweeps the previous candle and closes back inside its range
rules.setupAnchor: Use the previous candle's high and low as the reference range for the active Candle 2
rules.confirmationTrigger: Bullish Candle 2 sweeps the previous low and closes back above it, while bearish Candle 2 sweeps the previous high and closes back below it
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: The Candle 2 reversal creates the first valid swing reference only once the reversal closure is complete
rules.invalidationCondition: Price sweeps the previous candle but fails to close back inside the range or closes in continuation mode instead
rules.targetLogic: Treat the closure as the turning point that sets up Candle 3 continuation and later Candle 4 expansion if the sequence remains intact
exceptions: A continuation closure beyond the previous candle's high or low is not a Candle 2 closure even if the sweep occurred first
machineChecks: Detect sweep beyond the previous candle high or low
Require the Candle 2 close to finish back inside the previous candle range
Classify the event as bullish or bearish based on which side was swept and reclaimed

rules.name: A Candle 2 closure is only valid when it forms at a higher-timeframe point of interest
rules.setupAnchor: Map the active swing high or low, fair value gap, or fallback opposing candle before looking for the Candle 2 reversal closure
rules.confirmationTrigger: Only accept the Candle 2 closure when the reversal forms at the mapped point of interest and aligns with the higher-timeframe directional idea
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: The swing is ignored unless both ingredients exist: the point of interest and the valid Candle 2 closure
rules.invalidationCondition: A reversal closure appears away from the mapped point of interest or without higher-timeframe alignment
rules.targetLogic: Use the valid point of interest plus closure pair as the anchor for lower-timeframe confirmation and continuation into Candle 3
exceptions: If no swing high or low or fair value gap exists, an opposing candle can act as the fallback point of interest
machineChecks: Require a mapped point of interest before a Candle 2 closure can become actionable
Allow a fallback opposing-candle anchor only when no clearer higher-timeframe point of interest exists
Reject Candle 2 events that form without higher-timeframe alignment
ambiguityNotes: The fallback opposing-candle point of interest still needs a stricter first-pass ranking rule

rules.name: A valid Candle 2 closure should hand off to Candle 3 continuation in the new direction
rules.setupAnchor: Once Candle 2 closes as a reversal at the point of interest, use its range and directional shift as the new reference structure
rules.confirmationTrigger: Candle 3 expands beyond Candle 2 in the new direction and confirms that the reversal is transitioning into continuation
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: The Candle 2 turning point becomes the structural pivot that later continuation must protect while Candle 3 and Candle 4 develop
rules.invalidationCondition: Candle 3 fails to continue through Candle 2's directional edge or immediately disrespects the new turning point
rules.targetLogic: Use Candle 2 as the swing-turn anchor and Candle 3 as the continuation confirmation before anticipating Candle 4 expansion
exceptions: If Candle 3 does not continue, the model remains incomplete and should not be forced into a continuation read
machineChecks: Store the Candle 2 range after a valid reversal closure appears
Detect whether Candle 3 closes beyond Candle 2 in the new direction
Invalidate the sequence when Candle 3 cannot confirm the directional handoff

rules.name: Large-wick Candle 2 closures should keep Candle 3 above or below the wick midpoint to remain valid
rules.setupAnchor: Measure the full Candle 2 wick and mark its midpoint when Candle 2 prints a large rejection wick
rules.confirmationTrigger: Candle 3 should respect the Candle 2 wick midpoint in the direction of the new swing for the fractal model to remain intact
rules.protectedSwingDefinition: The midpoint filter helps separate strong turning points from weak swings that are unlikely to hold
rules.invalidationCondition: Candle 3 disrespects the Candle 2 wick midpoint and trades through the wrong side of the rejection
rules.targetLogic: Only keep the fractal sequence active when Candle 3 respects the midpoint and continues into the next expansion phase
exceptions: Midpoint filtering matters most when Candle 2 forms a visibly large rejection wick
machineChecks: Compute the Candle 2 wick midpoint from the rejection candle
Track whether Candle 3 respects the midpoint in the direction of the reversal
Downgrade the setup when midpoint respect fails before continuation develops
ambiguityNotes: The minimum wick size that deserves midpoint filtering is not yet numeric

openQuestions: What is the first useful numeric tolerance for saying Candle 3 respected versus disrespected the Candle 2 wick midpoint?
How should the fallback opposing-candle point of interest be ranked against clearer swing or fair-value-gap anchors?
